READ THE LAUREATE

How a cubic kilometre of ice became a telescope

IceCube and the Discovery of High-Energy Cosmic Neutrinos · Francis Halzen

This compact lecture traces the wager behind IceCube: use clear Antarctic ice and thousands of light sensors to turn almost invisible cosmic neutrinos into a new view of the high-energy universe.

01

Why build so large?

Neutrinos interact so rarely that discovery requires an instrumented volume on the scale of a cubic kilometre.

02

Ice becomes optics

Charged particles born in a neutrino collision emit Cherenkov light; its timing and pattern reconstruct direction and energy.

03

A new cosmic messenger

High-energy neutrinos point toward violent sources that ordinary light alone cannot fully reveal.

WHY IT MATTERS

The universe sends messengers

Neutrinos travel through matter almost undisturbed. IceCube turns a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a detector, tracing rare flashes back to energetic cosmic sources.

Verified source ↗
INPUT High-energy cosmic neutrinos
PROCESS Cherenkov light captured deep in Antarctic ice
OUTPUT Direction, energy, and astrophysical source clues
